title: GCZRec: Generative Collaborative Zero-Shot Framework for Cold Start News Recommendation
authors: Hassan, S.Z.U.; Rafi, M.; Frnda, J.
tldr: A generative collaborative zero-shot recommender system uses dual conditional Wasserstein GANs and zero-shot classifiers to synthesize user-item interactions for cold start news recommendation.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional collaborative filtering fails when historical interaction data is unavailable, as in cold start news items posted without prior user engagement. Existing content-based and deep learning approaches do not leverage latent collaborative information between users and items simultaneously, limiting serendipity and diversity in recommendations. The cold start problem in news recommendation is particularly acute due to the rapid publication pace of new articles.
approach: Formulates cold start recommendation as a zero-shot classification task, predicting labels for unseen users and items from their latent feature representations.
Designs dual generator networks implemented as conditional Wasserstein GANs (cWGANs) for news-to-user and user-to-news interaction synthesis.
Trains two independent 1D-CNN classifiers as zero-shot predictors for novel news items and users based on hierarchical clustering of latent features.
Evaluates on two public datasets: Microsoft News Dataset (MIND) and Addressa, under both exclusively cold start and mixed cold-warm start settings.
Compares against GAZRec-NPA, GNUD, and NAML baselines using AUC, nDCG@k, and MAP metrics.
findings: GCZRec achieves highest AUC and ranking quality on MIND dataset in cold start settings, outperforming GAZRec-NPA, GNUD, and NAML.
num: Average improvement of +0.1113 in nDCG@k when top-5 items are considered, demonstrating superior ranking quality.
MAP scores show significant improvement in mixed warm-cold start cases compared to purely cold start items.
The framework generates diverse recommendations by implicitly leveraging collaborative signals between similar users and items.
The model can serve as a preprocessing module to enhance existing recommender system performance.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces GCZRec, a novel generative framework that reformulates the cold start recommendation problem as zero-shot learning. By using dual conditional Wasserstein GANs with zero-shot classifiers, the framework synthesizes user-item interactions without requiring historical data for novel users or items. The approach uniquely leverages collaborative signals implicitly during training to produce diverse and serendipitous recommendations. Experiments on MIND and Addressa demonstrate competitive or superior performance compared to existing cold start baselines.
directly_justifies: Cold start problem can be effectively modeled as zero-shot classification using latent feature representations.
Dual generator networks can synthesize realistic user-item interactions without historical data.
Collaborative signals between users and items improve recommendation diversity and serendipity.
The framework achieves highest ranking quality with nDCG improvement of +0.1113 over baselines.
limits: Does not consider temporal relationships between news clicks and item correlations.
Underperforms on Addressa dataset in mixed cold-warm start case, possibly due to label encoding.
Limited to news recommendation; generalizability to other domains not demonstrated.
No evaluation of computational cost or inference latency compared to baselines.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) is highly relevant through 5.B as the paper directly addresses the cold-start problem for new users and items. Code 5.C is moderately relevant since the zero-shot classification approach parallels behavioral profile prediction. Domain 11 (Engagement Dynamics) is low-relevant through 11.A given the discussion of serendipity and user engagement in recommendations. Domains 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, and 14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial practices, expense categorization, budgeting, predictive finance, anomaly detection, mobile design, privacy, evaluation of financial systems, savings, or synthetic data for ML.

limitations: Does not model temporal dependencies between news clicks or correlations between news items.
Performance degrades on Addressa in mixed cold-warm start compared to baselines.
Limited to news domain; applicability to financial recommendation systems not explored.
Computational cost and inference latency are not compared against baseline models.
